page.layout: One column of running text, with two short marginal notes in the right margin beside the first paragraph. Running head at the top, page number 25 at the top right, catchword "fini-" at the bottom right.

main_text.p: prosperis aliorum successibus contristari, atque dolere. Idque secundum illud Chryso-Chrysost. Homil. 26. in 2. Corinth.stomi versi: Heri & pridie amicus & loquebaris cum illo, fortasse et jam comedebas; repente cum videas membrum tuum magis honestatum, abjectâ amicitiæ personâ, hostilem induisti, imo insaniam. Insania enim est alienis bonis cruciari. Alii non justâ æmulatione vel ipsum victorem provocabunt; infausto duello experimentum sumpturi, num eodem animo in re seriâ fit futurus, quo in lu-do equestri, tam si certetur armis decretoriis, quam si ludicris. Adeoque non tantum corpori sed etiam animæ grande creabunt præjudicium.
Quod si nondum movent allegatæ hactenus rationes, saltem moveant exempla. Quis ignorat ista lætitiæ ac voluptatis simulacra ut plurimum dubia, ac luctuosa fuisse, casu quo fini-

page.notes: Chrysost. / Homil. 26. in 2. Corinth. are the right-margin references beside the first paragraph; they are placed as one note. Long s is read as s throughout. The hyphen in "Chryso-" and "lu-do" is printed. Some letters near the ink blots at "vel ipsum" and "infausto" are faint but read with reasonable confidence. The word "feriâ" was read as "seriâ" after the printed f, which has the form of a long s, so it is marked as read; no [?] was needed.
